title: Director of Finance and Administration
description:
Director of Finance and Administration

Organization: Malawi Council for Disability Affairs (MACODA)

Location: Blantyre, MalawiApply URL: https://careersmw.com/?post_type=job_listing&p=212291

The Malawi Council for Disability Affairs (MACODA) a Statutory Corporation established by an Act of Parliament, the Persons with Disabilities act (No. 4 of 2024), to protect and promote fundamental rights and freedoms of persons with disabilities. MACODA is an enforcement agency of the Act and is particularly legally mandated to investigate and carry out inquiries into violations of rights of persons with disabilities. Among the Council’s functions for disability programming and steering disability mainstreaming in the Malawi’s development include promoting multisectoral coordination and collaboration; development of standards and guidelines on a rights-based for disability service provision; regulating disability services and programmes; promotion of measures and interventions aimed at promoting realisation of rights of persons with disabilities and registration of persons with disabilities as well as organisations, associations and institutions implementing disability programmes including those that provide specialised services to persons with disabilities. Applications are invited from suitably qualified candidates to fill the two key positions of Director of Finance & Administration and Director of Rehabilitation Services. The position is tenable at MACODA Head Office on Kittermaster Avenue, BCA Hills, Limbe DIRECTOR OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION GRADE: MCD 2 THE JOB PURPOSE The Director of Finance and Administration (DFA) is the Head of Finance and Administration at MACODA and reports directly to the Director General of MACODA. The DFA’s main responsibility is to devise an efficient financial system and to provide Human Resource and Administrative support services to the core operations of the Council. In addition to regular financial management and day to day Human Resource and Administrative functions, the DFA forms part of Council’s Senior Management Team and as such shall be expected to participate in the development of appropriate policies and procedures to enhance Council’s operational efficiency. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES The successful candidate shall be expected to: Managing the Finance and Administration Department and providing overall leadership, guidance and direction in the planning and execution of all finance and administrative functions of the Council. Developing, implementing and maintaining sound financial management and control systems of MACODA, including maintaining Councils Computerized accounting system. Formulating, implementing and constantly reviewing financial policies and procedures of MACODA. Formulating criteria for fund management and implementation of fund allocation and disbursement for Councils Units. Preparing monthly management accounts and producing quarterly and annual accounts in compliance with the generally acceptable accounting procedures and practices. Managing Councils fixed assets and insurance portfolios. Managing the human resource and administrative functions including overseeing the preparation and payment of monthly staff salaries, the recruitment and supervision of middle management and support staff, and conducting periodic job evaluations and staff performance reviews and appraisals. Developing and implementing staff development plans. Coordinating the development and management of Councils annual budget. QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES The successful candidate will have a Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting or Business Administration. Chartered Accountants or those with Masters degrees in Finance Management, Accounting, Business Administration will have an added advantage. He/She shall have requisite experience in Human Resource Management and Administration A minimum of three years of work experience at senior management level preferably in a reputable organization. Excellent communication and negotiation skills. Sound Management and interpersonal skills. Computer literacy and team spirit. REMUNERATION-PACKAGE The successful candidates shall be offered a negotiated performance related contract for a period of Three (3) years with an attractive salary, benefits and gratuity package commensurate with the seniority of the position. METHOD OF APPLICATION Interested candidates should submit their applications with detailed Curriculum Vitae, names and contact details of three traceable referees to: The Comptroller of Statutory Corporations P.O BOX 30061 Capital City LILONGWE 3. Closing date for receipt of application letters is 24th August, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be acknowledged. Women and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply!

title: Intermodal &#038; Logistics Manager
description:
Intermodal & Logistics Manager

Organization: Careers Consulting Limited

Location: Blantyre, MalawiApply URL: https://careersmw.com/?post_type=job_listing&p=212284

A premier global leader in container shipping and logistics is seeking a highly qualified Intermodal & Logistics Manager Management Level: Middle Management Reports to: Commercial Director Job Location: Blantyre, Malawi Purpose of the Job The Intermodal & Logistics Manager is responsible for leading, coordinating and improving the company’s inland transport, depot and logistics activities for containerised import and export cargo. The role ensures that containers move efficiently, safely and cost-effectively across road, rail, port and inland depot corridors, while maintaining high customer service standards, accurate reporting, strong vendor performance and profitable intermodal operations. The position is especially focused on strengthening hinterland operations, improving service delivery for key export and import customers, reducing demurrage and detention exposure, ensuring accurate container tracking, and supporting the growth of value-added logistics services linked to a liner shipping business. Key Responsibilities 1. Intermodal Operations Management Plan, coordinate and monitor pre-carriage and on-carriage container movements between inland origins, customers, depots, border points and ports. Manage road, rail and multimodal solutions to ensure cargo is delivered on time and in line with customer commitments. Ensure close alignment between inland movements, vessel schedules, port cut-offs, equipment availability and customer loading or delivery requirements. Monitor container status from release through loading, dispatch, border crossing, port arrival, empty return and final closure. Proactively identify operational risks, delays, congestion, missed cut-offs or equipment shortages, and implement corrective actions. 2. Logistics, Depot and Equipment Coordination Oversee depot activities related to container lift-in, lift-out, grounding, shunting, storage, empty returns, upgrades, repairs and inspections. Coordinate with Equipment Control to maintain container availability for exports and to reduce costly empty repositioning. Support efficient use of inland depot capacity and ensure visibility of full and empty containers across the network. Ensure container maintenance, cleaning, upgrading and inspection activities are properly arranged, recorded and charged where applicable. Work with internal teams to improve import and export documentation flow linked to intermodal movements. 3. Vendor and Transporter Management Develop, maintain and manage relationships with trucking companies, rail operators, inland depots, terminals, clearing agents and other logistics service providers. With the Commercial Director, negotiate competitive and sustainable transport, depot and handling rates in line with company pricing strategy and service requirements. Measure vendor performance against agreed service levels, including truck availability, on-time pickup and delivery, communication quality, safety compliance and cost control. Implement corrective actions with underperforming vendors and maintain a reliable panel of approved service providers. Ensure transporters provide timely truck details, status updates, proof of delivery and exception reports. 4. Commercial Support and Customer Service Support the commercial team with inland logistics solutions, pricing inputs, customer proposals and operational feasibility assessments. Provide reliable updates to customers on container movements, delivery schedules, delays, documentation requirements and exception handling. Assist in developing tailored logistics solutions for key containerised cargo segments, including agricultural exports, industrial imports and project cargo where applicable. Participate in customer meetings when operational or intermodal expertise is required. Ensure service failures are investigated, communicated and resolved in a professional and timely manner. 5. Reporting, Revenue and Cost Control Prepare accurate weekly and monthly intermodal reports, including volumes, revenue, margins, container forecasts, outstanding movements, demurrage exposure and operational exceptions. Ensure all intermodal revenue, costs, margins, recoveries and charges are correctly captured, validated and reported. Monitor demurrage, detention, storage and delay costs, and take preventive action to reduce avoidable charges. Review transport and depot invoices against agreed rates, services performed and supporting documentation. Identify opportunities to improve profitability through better routing, pricing, vendor negotiation, asset utilisation and process control. 6. Compliance, Risk and Safety Ensure inland transport operations comply with applicable customs, road transport, rail, port, safety, insurance and company requirements. Maintain proper documentation for bonded movements, customs clearance, container releases, transporter instructions and customer delivery requirements. Promote safe handling of containers and cargo across depots, terminals and transport partners. Escalate high-risk operational issues, claims, cargo incidents, equipment damage or service failures to management promptly. Support internal and external audits by maintaining accurate operational records and evidence. 7. Team Leadership and Process Improvement Lead, coach and support intermodal, logistics and documentation team members to ensure high performance and accountability. Allocate daily responsibilities, monitor workloads and ensure priority shipments are followed up effectively. Develop standard operating procedures for inland transport, reporting, demurrage control, customer updates and exception handling. Drive continuous improvement by reducing manual work, improving data accuracy, strengthening communication and increasing operational visibility. Build a culture of ownership, urgency, service excellence and cost awareness within the team. Key Performance Indicators On-time pickup and delivery performance for inland container movements. Accuracy and timeliness of container tracking and operational reporting. Reduction in avoidable demurrage, detention, storage and delay costs. Intermodal revenue growth, margin control and cost recovery performance. Vendor performance against agreed service levels and cost targets. Customer satisfaction and responsiveness on logistics and intermodal matters. Accuracy of rate application, invoicing support and revenue reporting. Operational compliance with customs, safety, documentation and company procedures. Key Stakeholders & Interface (Optional) Internal Commercial, Customer Service, Documentation, Imports, Exports, Equipment Control, Finance, Operations, Management and regional intermodal teams. External Customers, transporters, rail operators, port terminals, inland depots, clearing agents, customs authorities, insurers and other logistics service providers Minimum Qualifications & Experience Bachelor’s degree or diploma in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Transport Management, Maritime Studies, Business Administration or a related field. Minimum of 10 years’ experience in logistics, intermodal transport, liner shipping, freight forwarding, inland haulage, rail, depot or supply chain operations. At least 3 years’ experience in a management role is preferred. Strong knowledge of containerised cargo operations, inland transport planning, depot activities, import and export processes and port interfaces. Experience working with transporters, clearing agents, terminals, depots, rail operators and shipping line systems. Sound commercial understanding of freight pricing, cost control, demurrage, detention, storage, margins and vendor negotiation. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, especially Excel and Outlook; experience with shipping, transport management, ERP or reporting systems will be an advantage. Required Skills & Competencies Strong planning, coordination and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities. Commercially minded, with a strong focus on cost control, profitability and customer service. Ability to work under pressure, manage urgent shipments and make timely decisions. High attention to detail, especially in reporting, tracking, invoicing and documentation. Strong negotiation skills and the ability to manage service providers effectively. Leadership capability with the ability to develop, motivate and hold teams accountable. Integrity, professionalism and commitment to compliance, safety and company values. Notes Description may not reflect the full details of every aspect of a job; specific tasks may be assigned by the direct manager. Management has the sole responsibility of defining the limits and scope of all jobs in the organization and determining the suitability of a candidate or existing employee for a role. Changes to the job description can only be made by the direct manager and must be approved by both the Managing Director and HR. Once approved, the latest version becomes the only valid copy for use. Distribution of copies: Job Holder, Direct Manager, and HR records. The HR copy is the one acknowledged in writing by the Job Holder. Office-based role with regular operational follow-up and travel to customers, depots, and service providers as required. May require availability outside normal working hours to resolve urgent operational issues, vessel cut-off risks, customer escalations or transport disruptions. Requires regular interaction with cross-border stakeholders and the ability to manage fast-changing transport and shipping conditions. How to apply Applicants meeting the requirements are encouraged to send their Cover Letter, Updated CV and Relevant Certifications, in Pdf format , through email to jobs@careersmw.com . Please ensure your gender is indicated on your CV. Each file should be sent separately -No Zip Files are allowed. Please use the subject line “ Intermodal & Logistics Manager – Your Name ,” and ensure that each file is appropriately labelled, such as “CV – (Name)” Please note that incomplete applications will not be considered. The closing date for receiving applications is Thursday, 14th August 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

The DRS reports to the Director General and is responsible for coordinating, monitoring and evaluation of rehabilitation programmes and services. The DRS forms part of MACODA’s Senior Management Team and as such shall be expected to participate in the development of appropriate policies and procedures to enhance the operational efficiency of the Council. Maintaining contact with various relevant public and private organizations concerned with the rights, care and welfare of persons with disabilities for effective networking and implementation of rehabilitation programmes and services. Support the Council’s mobilization of resources for the delivery of rehabilitation programmes and services. Conducting day to day management and supervision of rehabilitation staff. Creating a conducive environment for optimum (rehabilitation) staff development and output. Preparation of rehabilitation department’s annual estimates and control of the budget. Collation of departmental reports for the consumption of the Board and other relevant stakeholders. Four (5) years working experience in the disability related field. Excellent communication and negotiation skills. Sound management and interpersonal skills. Ability to develop proposals for implementation of disability rights projects. In-depth practical familiarity with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD). Knowledge of local and international disability rights instruments. Demonstrable knowledge of emerging disability issues in Malawi.
